rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathered beings cannot address God about His judgment by objection or intercession; address also covers other means of escaping harm, such as ransom, friendship, prayer, and supplication.
rows.anchor: المراد به أنهم لا يملكون أن يخاطبوه فيما يقضي ويفعل بهم باعتراض عليه أو شفاعة فيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels are honored servants who never object to God, and the Spirit is His true word; truth does not oppose or contradict truth.
rows.anchor: عباد مكرمون لا يسبقونه بالقول وهم بأمره يعملون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject of they do not possess is everyone gathered for Judgment: angels, the Spirit, humans, and jinn, rather than only angels and the Spirit or only tyrants.
rows.anchor: لجميع المجموعين ليوم الفصل من الملائكة والروح والإنس والجن كما هو المناسب للسياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Restricting the subject to angels and the Spirit lacks prior mention, while restricting it to tyrants is too remote from the context.
rows.anchor: دون خصوص الملائكة والروح لعدم سبق الذكر ودون خصوص الطاغين كما قيل لكثرة الفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase when the Spirit and angels stand in ranks is an adverbial for they do not possess; attaching it to they do not speak is a distant reading.
rows.anchor: ظرف لقوله { لا يملكون } ، وقيل لقوله { لا يتكلمون } وهو بعيد مع صلاحية ظرفيته لما سبقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Spirit is the created being belonging to the divine command, as in the verse saying that the Spirit is from the Lord's command.
rows.anchor: المخلوق الأمري الذي يشير إليه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported interpretation identifies the Spirit as the most eminent angels; the author says there is no evidence for this or the following identifications.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد به اشراف الملائكة، وقيل حفظة الملائكة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation identifies the Spirit as the guardian angels.
rows.anchor: وقيل حفظة الملائكة وقيل ملك موكل على الأرواح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation identifies the Spirit as an angel assigned to human souls.
rows.anchor: وقيل ملك موكل على الأرواح. ولا دليل على شيء من هذه الأقوال.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported interpretation identifies the Spirit as Gabriel.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد به جبريل، وقيل أرواح الناس وقيامها مع الملائكة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported interpretation takes the Spirit to mean human spirits standing with the angels between the two blasts, before entering bodies.
rows.anchor: وقيل أرواح الناس وقيامها مع الملائكة صفا إنما هو بين النفختين قبل أن تلج الأجساد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported interpretation takes the Spirit as the Quran, whose effects appear that day in believers' happiness and disbelievers' misery.
rows.anchor: وقيل القرآن والمراد من قيامه ظهور آثاره يومئذ من سعادة المؤمنين به وشقاوة الكافرين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel, human spirits, and the Quran are called Spirit elsewhere with a qualifier, whereas this verse uses the term without one; the final two readings are also arbitrary.
rows.anchor: ويدفعها أن هذه الثلاثة وإن أطلق على كل منها الروح في كلامه تعالى لكنه مع التقييد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other Quranic uses call these three things Spirit with qualifiers, but the Spirit here is unqualified; identifying it with either of the last two views is especially arbitrary.
rows.anchor: والروح في الآية التي نحن فيها مطلق، على أن في القولين الأخيرين تحكما ظاهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Safan is a circumstantial expression derived from a verbal noun and means that they are lined up.
rows.anchor: حال من الروح والملائكة وهو مصدر أريد به اسم الفاعل أي حال كونهم صافين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between the Spirit and the angels may suggest that the Spirit stands alone in one rank while all the angels form another.
rows.anchor: وربما استفيد من مقابة الروح للملائكة أن الروح وحده صف والملائكة جميعا صف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do not speak explains they do not possess speech, and its subject is all gathered beings, as the context indicates.
rows.anchor: بيان لقوله { لا يملكون منه خطابا } وضمير الفاعل لأهل الجمع من الروح والملائكة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other readings restrict the pronoun in they do not speak to the Spirit and angels, or to people; neither fits the parallel wording and context.
rows.anchor: وقيل الضمير للروح والملائكة، وقيل للناس ووقوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Except whom the Merciful permits is appositional to the subject of they do not speak and identifies those allowed to speak at all; it parallels the general permission in Hud 105.
rows.anchor: أريد به بيان من له أن يتكلم منهم يومئذ بإذن الله فالجملة في معنى قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Said what is right means speech free of error or falsehood, and functions as a condition on permission: God permits only one who speaks rightly.
rows.anchor: قال قولا صوابا لا يشوبه خطأ وهو الحق الذي لا يداخله باطل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes the exception as those for whom intercession is made and rightness as professing monotheism in earthly life; it parallels the verse on intercession for those God approves.
rows.anchor: استثناء ممن يتكلم فيه والمراد بالصواب التوحيد وقول لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative is unlikely because the passage denies that anyone can speak at all, rather than allowing speech but restricting the people for whom it is made.
rows.anchor: العناية الكلامية في المقام متعلقة بنفي أصل الخطاب والتكلم يومئذ من كل متكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran uses Spirit for a principle of life without limiting it to humans or to humans and animals; it also affirms a Spirit in other beings.
rows.anchor: ولم يقصرها في الإنسان أو في الإنسان والحيوان فحسب بل أثبتها في غيرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quranic definition identifies the Spirit as belonging to God's command; that command is God's bringing a thing into being by saying Be.
rows.anchor: حيث أطلقها إطلاقا وذكر معرفا لها أنها من أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh gathered his subjects forcefully; the following call that he was their highest lord shows that the gathering concerned all his realm.
rows.anchor: الحشر جمع الناس بإزعاج والمراد به جمعه الناس من أهل مملكته كما يدل عليه تفريع قوله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported view says Pharaoh gathered the magicians, citing the gathering of summoners and his assembling his plot elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالحشر جمع السحرة لقوله تعالى فأرسل فرعون في المدائن حاشرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited verses do not prove that the gathering here has the same meaning as the gathering there.
rows.anchor: وفيه أنه لا دليل على كون المراد بالحشر في هذه الآية هو عين المراد بالحشر والجمع في تينك الآيتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh claims divinity and, on the apparent meaning, ranks himself above the other gods acknowledged by his polytheistic people.
rows.anchor: وظاهره أنه يدعي أنه أعلى في الربوبية من سائر الأرباب التي كان يقول بها قومه الوثنيون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may have meant that he was the most proximate deity, controlling people's provisions and affairs and preserving their honor, unlike the other gods.
rows.anchor: أنه أقرب الآلهة منهم تجري بيده أرزاقهم وتصلح بأمره شؤون حياتهم ويحفظ بمشيئته شرفهم وسؤددهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view reads the boast as political supremacy over officials and governors, effectively a claim to kingship, like his boast about Egypt's kingdom.
rows.anchor: وقيل مراده بما قال تفضيل نفسه على كل من يلي أمورهم ومحصله دعوى الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The political reading conflicts with the apparent wording and Pharaoh's explicit claims that no god exists for his people besides him.
rows.anchor: وهو خلاف ظاهر الكلام وفيما قال قوله لملإه يا أيها الملأ ما علمت لكم من إله غيري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's taking Pharaoh is a figure for punishing him; nakal is deterrent punishment, and both worldly destruction and afterlife punishment deter others.
rows.anchor: الأخذ كناية عن التعذيب، والنكال التعذيب الذي يردع من رآه أو سمعه عن تعاطي مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The former and latter refer to this world and the Hereafter: Pharaoh and his troops drowned here, and he faces punishment after death.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بالأولى والآخرة الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes the latter as Pharaoh's final boast and the former as his earlier claim that he knew no god besides himself, making both utterances the cause of his punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالآخرة كلمته الآخرة، { أنا ربكم الأعلى } وبالأولى كلمته الأولى قالها قبل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation that the two terms designate Pharaoh's two statements is obscure.
rows.anchor: ولا يخلو هذا المعنى من خفاء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reading takes the first as Pharaoh's denial and disobedience at the beginning of the story and the latter as his final boast.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالأولى تكذيبه ومعصيته المذكوران في أول القصة وبالأخرى كلمة - أنا ربكم الأعلى - المذكورة في آخرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading that the terms refer to the beginning and ending of the story is likewise obscure.
rows.anchor: وهو كسابقه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view means the first and last of Pharaoh's sins, so God punished him for their totality.
rows.anchor: وقيل الاولى أول معاصيه والأخرى آخرها والمعنى أخذه الله نكال مجموع معاصيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation that the two terms mean the first and last of all his sins is also obscure.
rows.anchor: ولا يخلو أيضا من خفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story of Moses is an admonition for anyone disposed by sound human nature to fear misery and punishment; the object of fear is left unstated.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن مفعول { يخشى } منسي معرض عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each person's overwhelming concern keeps him from attending to anyone else, which explains why people flee from even their closest relatives.
rows.anchor: أي يكفيه من أن يشتغل بغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposed reasons for a person fleeing relatives and intimates that day have no evidence, so the author omits them.
rows.anchor: وقيل في سبب فرار الانسان من أقربائه وأخصائه يومئذ وجوه أخر لا دليل عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Radiant, laughing, joyful faces identify the blessed group; brightness and gladness show their happiness and the sight of good news.
rows.anchor: إسفار الوجه إشراقه وإضاءته فرحا وسرورا واستبشاره تهلله بمشاهدة ما فيه البشرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dust and gloom on faces are signs of anxiety and grief.
rows.anchor: هي الغبار والكدورة وهي سيماء الهم والغم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covering darkness means blackness and gloom overtaking the faces; the face mirrors the heart's joy or sorrow.
rows.anchor: أي يعلوها ويغشاها سواد وظلمة، وقد بين حال الطائفتين في الآيات الأربع ببيان حال وجوههما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second group combines disbelief in belief with grave disobedience in conduct; the warning focuses on them, so the blessed group is not similarly labeled.
rows.anchor: أي الجامعون بين الكفر اعتقادا والفجور وهو المعصية الشنيعة عملا أو الكافرون بنعمة الله الفاجرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also allows the sense of people who deny God's favor and act wickedly.
rows.anchor: أو الكافرون بنعمة الله الفاجرون

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن يزيد
rows.claim: A man asked Umar what abban means; when people kept discussing it, Umar came at them with his whip.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن يزيد أن رجلا سأل عمر عن قوله { وأبا } فلما رآهم يقولون أقبل عليهم بالدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report reflects an effort to stop people from investigating the Book's meanings, even its vocabulary.
rows.anchor: هو مبني على منعهم عن البحث عن معارف الكتاب حتى تفسير ألفاظه

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
rows.claim: In a report from al-Irshad, Abu Bakr says he knows the meaning of fruit but not abban, and fears making an unsupported claim about God's Book.
rows.anchor: فلم يعرف معنى الأب من القرآن فقال أي سماء تظلني أم أي أرض تقلني

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام
rows.claim: Ali explains that abban is pasture and that the verse counts God's gifts of food for people and livestock, sustaining their lives and bodies.
rows.anchor: أما علم أن الأب هو الكلاء والمرعى

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Qummi glosses each person's overwhelming concern as an occupation that keeps him from anyone else.
rows.anchor: قال شغل يشغله عن غيره

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says people will be resurrected barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised, submerged in sweat to their earlobes; they will be too absorbed to notice one another.
rows.anchor: " عن سودة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قالت قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah recalls Judgment through its signs and events, then says human deeds will be exposed and the Quran is conveyed by an angel, not Satan; it also rejects the charge that the Prophet is mad.
rows.anchor: تذكر السورة يوم القيامة بذكر بعض أشراطها وما يقع فيها وتصفه بأنه يوم ينكشف فيه للإنسان ما عمله من عمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its defense of the Prophet against an early accusation of madness suggests an early Meccan date, as does the early surah Nun's similar defense; the surah is unquestionably Meccan.
rows.anchor: ويشبه أن تكون السورة من السور العتائق النازلة في أوائل البعثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takwir means wrapping or coiling like a turban; the sun's takwir likely metaphorically describes its body darkening in an enveloping way.
rows.anchor: التكوير اللف على طريق الإدارة كلف العمامة على الرأس، ولعل المراد بتكوير الشمس انظلام جرمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inkidar may describe stars plunging from the sky toward earth, hence falling, as in the verse about scattered stars.
rows.anchor: انكدار الطائر من الهواء انقضاضه نحو الأرض، وعليه فالمراد سقوط النجوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, inkidar means change or clouding, so the stars lose their light.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون من الانكدار بمعنى التغير وقبول الكدورة فيكون المراد به ذهاب ضوئها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour's earthquake moves the mountains, crushes them into scattered dust, and makes them a mirage, as described elsewhere in the Quran.
rows.anchor: فتندك وتكون هباء منبثا وتصير سرابا على ما ذكره سبحانه في مواضع من كلامه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The ten-month camels are pregnant camels that have reached ten months; they were among the Arabs' most prized property.
rows.anchor: العشار جمع عشراء كالنفاس جمع نفساء وهي الناقة الحامل التي أتت عليها عشرة أشهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaving these camels unattended alludes to prized wealth having no owner or caretaker because people are consumed by their own affairs.
rows.anchor: وتعطيل العشار تركها مهملة لا راعي لها ولا حافظ يحفظها وكأن في الجملة إشارة على نحو الكناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wild animals are creatures unaccustomed to humans, including predators and others; in this Judgment context they too are gathered as humans are.
rows.anchor: الوحوش جمع وحش وهو من الحيوان ما لا يتأنس بالإنسان كالسباع وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity's finest form and all its arrangements depend on the generous Lord's governance; humans have no hand in them.
rows.anchor: والجميع ينتهي إلى تدبير الرب الكريم لا صنع للانسان في شيء من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No indeed rebukes people for using God's generosity as an excuse for heedlessness; their supposed confidence does not save them.
rows.anchor: ردع عن اغترار الانسان بكرم الله وجعل ذلك ذريعة إلى الكفر والمعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rather, you deny the recompense means that the addressees, and anyone like them, persistently reject the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: أي بالجزاء. إضراب عما يفهم من قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deeds are preserved for Judgment by angels writing a record, separately from their presence in a person's memory, so the person can be reckoned by it.
rows.anchor: حفظها بكتابة كتاب الأعمال من الملائكة الموكلين بالإنسان فيحاسب عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guardians are noble and honored by God; the Quran repeatedly calls angels noble, and this may also mean they are created immune to sin and disobedience.
rows.anchor: أولي كرامة وعزة عند الله تعالى وقد تكرر في القرآن الكريم وصف الملائكه بالكرامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference to writing means recording deeds, as indicated by the following phrase that they know what people do.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالكتابة في قوله { كاتبين } كتابة الأعمال بقرينة قوله { يعلمون ما تفعلون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What makes you know the Day of Judgment magnifies it: its reality exceeds human comprehension and description; explicitly repeating day instead of using a pronoun heightens the emphasis.
rows.anchor: تهويل وتفخيم لأمر يوم الدين، والمعنى لا تحيط علما بحقيقة يوم الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the question about the Day of Judgment intensifies the warning and magnification.
rows.anchor: في تكرار الجملة تأكيد للتفخيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day phrase is an object of an implied remember, and gives an overall account of the Judgment whose reality the preceding verses urged people to know.
rows.anchor: الظرف منصوب بتقدير اذكر ونحوه، وفي الآية بيان إجمالي لحقيقة يوم الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That day, causal influence between apparent causes and their effects ends; no soul can ward off harm or bring good for another.
rows.anchor: رابطة التأثير والتأثر بين الأسباب الظاهرية ومسبباتها منقطعة زائلة يومئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This does not rule out intercession, which exists only by God's permission and belongs to Him alone.
rows.anchor: ولا ينافي ذلك آيات الشفاعة لأنها بإذن الله المالك لها لا غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone owns all command and none besides Him has any share in it.
rows.anchor: أي هو المالك للأمر ليس لغيره من الأمر شيء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative derives command as one of God's orders, fitting a sovereign's commands; interpreting it as affairs or circumstances fits the context less well.
rows.anchor: والمراد بامر كما قيل واحد الأوامر لقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi explains that the graves split open and people emerge from them.
rows.anchor: قال تنشق فتخرج الناس منها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says whoever begins a good or evil practice receives the equivalent reward or sin of those who follow it, without reducing their shares; Hudhayfa recited the verse about deeds sent ahead and left behind.
rows.anchor: من استن خيرا فاستن به فله أجره ومثل أجور من اتبعه غير منتقص من أجورهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report reaching Salih ibn Mismar says the Prophet recited the question about what deluded a person regarding his generous Lord, then answered that it was ignorance.
rows.anchor: عن صالح بن مسمار قال بلغني أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم تلا هذه الآية

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi explains that God could have composed a person in a form other than the one he has.
rows.anchor: قال لو شاء ركبك على غير هذه الصورة

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Majma transmits the same explanation from Ja'far al-Sadiq in a disconnected report.
rows.anchor: ورواه في المجمع عن الصادق عليه السلام مرسلا

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi identifies the guardians as the two angels appointed over each person.
rows.anchor: { وإن عليكم لحافظين } قال الملكان الموكلان بالإنسان

rows.speaker: غير مسمى
rows.claim: A report says day and night recording angels exchange duty at dawn and sunset until death, then praise the righteous for good deeds or reproach wrongdoers and testify against them.
rows.anchor: وعن سعد السعود وفي رواية أنهما

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far says God's command belongs to Him that day and every day; when Judgment comes, rulers perish and only God remains ruler.
rows.anchor: في قوله تعالى { والأمر يومئذ لله } روى عمرو بن شمر عن جابر عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام أنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far means God's ownership is always true, but becomes manifest to sight on Judgment Day; the narration is exemplary, like the Quran's other claims of features exclusive to that day.
rows.anchor: مراده عليه السلام أن كون الأمر لله لا يختص بيوم القيامة بل الأمر لله دائما، وتخصيصه بيوم القيامة باعتبار ظهوره
